subject: Human Evolution
title: Persistence Hunting
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Persistence Hunting.

hook.text: Antelopes sprint faster than any human. But they overheat after a few minutes. We don't.

buildup.text: Humans sweat through millions of glands. Most mammals cool only by panting, which fails during a run.

discovery.text: Persistence hunting means chasing prey at a jog for hours until it collapses from heat exhaustion.

twist.text: San Bushmen still practice it today—running a kudu for four hours in midday heat until it drops.

climax.text: Our bodies are built for endurance, not speed. Long legs, short toes, and a nuchal ligament stabilize the head.

punchline.text: We couldn't outrun our prey. We outran its cooling system.

quiz.question: How does persistence hunting work?
options: Chasing prey until it overheats and collapses
